newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends at 35.69/70 a dlr, forwards ease.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends at 35.69/70 a dlr, forwards ease.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.695/705 per dollar on Monday, almost unchanged from the day's opening quotes, dealers said.
The day was marked by sustained dollar buying by the leading player in the market as well as several corporates. The rupee breached the 35.70 mark with deals at 35.71, they said.
"But supplies continued to be good, with FII (foreign institutional investors) money coming today," said a dealer.
He said the funds were for FIIs' purchases in Indian stock markets in end October.
The spot dollar demand was also exaggerated by the premia touching a six-month low in the forward dollar market. The annualised six- month premia touched a low of 5.75 on Monday.
"People are expecting premia to continue to soften," said a dealer at a foreign bank. He said many firms were buying dollars outright for their near-term requirements.
"The cost of carrying is almost zero today," he said.
Given the strong demand for dollars, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), was not in the market on Monday, dealers said.
RBI has been buying dollars in recent weeks to arrest an appreciation of the rupee.
"RBI's new support level will be 35.65 (compared to 35.60 in recent weeks)," said a dealer referring to RBI's buying price.
The forward premia continued to be soft, with six month annualised premium quoted at 5.75 percent, a six-month low, dealers said.
Some dealers at banks as well as private firms said the forward premia could slip further, close to 5.0 percent.
